calibration.note: Morning's gates were placed correctly and its narrative was wrong, and the split matters. The ADD gate at a settled 1H close above 79,640.7 FIRED: the 14:00Z bar closed 80,206.2, clearing the line by 565.5 points, and the second-stage 80,003.4 filter cleared on the same bar. The REDUCE gate at a settled close below 79,250.0 did NOT fire, but only by 26.7 points - the 12:00Z bar wicked to 78,907.4 and closed 79,276.7, so the two-bar reclaim clause was never even tested. That is the third gate in a row placed inside the half-ATR band that resolved inside the session, and it is now a rule rather than an observation. Where morning went wrong was the READ. It saw open interest down 1.63 percent into a rising price, called the rally short covering, declared the up-ladder spent because 'above 80,523.5 there is no mapped fuel', and acted on that by trimming 12 percent of the spot core at 79,370.0 with a TAKE_PROFIT decision box. Price then rose 1,115.8 points to 80,485.8 and printed 80,850.0, open interest reversed to +1.67 percent, funding flipped negative, and the market laid down two fresh short-side liquidation rungs at 80,500 and 80,750 exactly where morning said there was none. acting_helped is FALSE. The cost is small - roughly 0.32 USDT of forfeited upside on a 22.7 USDT trim, and the 1.01 USDT realized gain is the first this book has ever booked - but the lesson is not about size. The transferable finding: a FALLING open interest print during an impulse is a snapshot, not a verdict. Short covering is often the FIRST leg of a move that new money then joins; treating a single OI reading as proof the move is finished caused the desk to sell strength into what turned out to be a genuine trend day. The amendment: require TWO consecutive OI readings in the same direction before letting OI override a clean multi-timeframe trend signal, and never let an OI print alone downgrade a decision box from ADD to TAKE_PROFIT when the 1H frame is above all four EMAs in ascending order with a positive histogram - which it was.
